title: marketplace: install-local purge-sample-data always answers 500 DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE (looks up a bare "driver" service nothing registers) — and seed records carry no id to purge by
body:
QA-source: #21720 · platform-core.marketplace-install-local-lifecycle · acceptance[4]

Clause A5 of `platform-core.marketplace-install-local-lifecycle` (rev 1) fails in the 17.7 pre-release run #21720 (subject `251a7dd4`); verifier V4 re-derived it on two fresh boots: CONFIRMED, P2. Predates 17.6.0.

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase with `OS_CLOUD_URL=off` from a scratch copy (install-local caches under `{cwd}/.objectstack/installed-packages`).
2. `os package install examples/app-crm/dist/objectstack.json -r http://localhost:{port}` as admin → "Package installed"; `crm_account` has its seed rows.
3. Admin `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/com.example.crm/purge-sample-data {}`.

- Expected: `{deleted, skipped, errors}`, the seed rows gone and user-authored rows kept.
- Actual: `500 {"code":"DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE","message":"driver service unavailable — cannot purge."}`, nothing deleted; a following reseed answers 422 `RESEED_NO_ROWS` because the rows are still there.

## Mechanism

1. `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1704` calls `ctx.getService('driver')`. Drivers register only as `driver.{name}` (`packages/runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts:41`, `default-datasource-plugin.ts:183`); nothing registers a bare `driver`. The unit test `marketplace-install-local-heal.test.ts:114` mocks a bare `driver` the real kernel never has, so it stays green.
2. **Behind it (V4):** fixing the lookup alone would not make the purge work. It deletes by `rec.id` and counts an id-less record as skipped (`:1715-1717`); all 28 CRM seed records, in the artifact and in the cached ledger entry, have no `id` (they are keyed by `externalId`), so it would report 28 skipped / 0 deleted. It also calls the driver's `delete` directly, bypassing the ObjectQL engine (hooks, audit).

## Done when

Purge resolves the datasource the seed landed in through the engine, matches seed rows by their seed key, and a dogfood test drives it on a real boot.
